contents.name: Theorem 1.1: a time-dependent vector field of bounded velocity generates a diffeotopy
Theorem 1.2: a compactly supported time-dependent vector field generates an isotopy

contents.name: Exercise 9: the knotted line in R^3 is nontrivially knotted but isotopic to the straight line, with no ambient isotopy between them

contents.name: §6.2, Theorem 6.2.1 (Hirsch-Smale): the derivative map from immersions to bundle monomorphisms is a weak homotopy equivalence in the range stated
contents.reason: The immersion classification theorem is the predecessor DT-25 pair of this run; DT-27 consumes it and does not restate or reprove it.

contents.name: §6.2, Proposition 6.2.3 and Corollary 6.2.4: existence of an immersion is equivalent to a section condition on the associated Stiefel bundle; trivial tangent bundle gives an immersion into R^{2v}
contents.reason: Immersion existence theory belongs to the DT-25 page scaffolded earlier in this run.

contents.name: §6.2, Lemmas 6.2.5–6.2.7 and Theorem 6.2.10: the induction over disks, restrictions and open manifolds in the proof of the immersion theorem
contents.reason: These are the internal steps of the DT-25 Smale-Hirsch proof; they are scaffolded there and consumed here only through the theorem.

contents.name: §6.3, Proposition 6.3.1: a null-homotopic Whitney circle with opposite signs and dimension hypotheses bounds an embedded model disk disjoint from the two sheets in its interior
contents.reason: The clean-disk general-position lemma is scaffolded as part of DT-22; DT-27's disjunction proposition consumes it through the in-run item.

contents.name: §6.3, Theorem 6.3.2: the model deformation realises the Whitney move and removes a cancelling pair of intersections by a diffeotopy supported near the disk
contents.reason: The Whitney-move theorem is a DT-22 item of this run; DT-27 applies it to the two branch sheets of a self-transverse immersion.

contents.name: §6.3, Proposition 6.3.3: connected sum with a standard self-transverse immersion of S^n in R^{2n} introduces one transverse self-intersection of either sign, with normal bundle isomorphic to the tangent bundle
§6.3, Theorem 6.3.4: for V^n connected, M^{2n} simply connected and n≥3, every map V→M is homotopic to a smooth embedding
contents.reason: This combines the cancellation move with the introduction of extra self-intersections, a stronger statement than the design's removal proposition; the creation move is not scaffolded on this pair, which states only the disjunction direction.

contents.name: §6.3, Lemma 6.3.5: [φ]·[φ]=e(φ)+2I(φ) for a self-transverse immersion into a 2n-manifold, so 2I is determined by the regular homotopy class
§6.3, Theorem 6.3.6: every smooth n-manifold immerses in R^{2n-1}

§6.3, paragraph after 6.3.2: for n odd the sign of a self-intersection flips under interchange of the branches, so any pair can be cancelled when M is simply connected; non-orientable cases need only a parity count
§6.4, isovariant maps, Lemma 6.4.1 (equivariant classes of deleted-product maps correspond to isovariant germs of self-products)
contents.reason: The deleted-product dictionary is recorded, without proof, as the not-supplied boundary remark of this A page; it is not scaffolded as a proved item.

contents.name: §6.4, Lemma 6.4.2 and Proposition 6.4.3: the connectivity of the inclusion of Stiefel manifolds into spaces of skew maps
contents.reason: These homotopy-theoretic inputs serve only the deleted-product classification that this page does not build; they have no consumer among the DT-27 items.

contents.name: §6.4, Proposition 6.4.4 and Theorem 6.4.5: skew bundle maps correspond to isovariant germ maps, and in the metastable range immersions are classified by isovariant germ homotopy
contents.reason: The metastable immersion classification refines DT-25's theorem; the design assigns the immersion-level statement to DT-25 and this pair only records the embedding boundary.

contents.name: §6.4, Theorems 6.4.8–6.4.9: embeddings are classified up to diffeotopy by isovariant homotopy of the deleted product in the metastable range, following the Whitney-trick model
contents.reason: Recorded as the sourced, non-load-bearing boundary remark of this A page (no proof is supplied here).

contents.name: §6.4, opening paragraph: the metastable range 2m>3v+ε is contrasted with the stable range m>2v+ε

contents.name: §1: self-intersection set Σ(f) of a general-position map and the equivalence relations (ambient isotopy, isotopy, concordance, isoposition)
§1: ambient isotopy is stronger than isotopy; in the DIFF category or codimension ≥3 in PL/TOP the two agree
§2, General Position Theorem 2.1.a: every n-polyhedron or n-manifold embeds in R^{2n+1} and unknots in R^m for m≥2n+2
contents.reason: The embedding half is already published as the weak Whitney embedding theorem on the DG page; the unknotting half is stable-range embedding uniqueness beyond this pair's scope.

contents.name: §2, Theorem 2.2.a: every n-manifold embeds in R^{2n} (Whitney), proved by general position and the Whitney trick
§2, Theorem 2.2.b: every connected n-manifold unknots in R^{2n+1} for n>1
contents.reason: Stable-range unknotting is not needed by the design's items; the pair stops at the primary obstruction, the disjunction lemma and the recorded Haefliger-Weber boundary.

contents.name: §2, Theorems 2.3.a-c: embeddability into R^{2n-1} and R^{2n-2} under orientability, connectivity and characteristic-class hypotheses
contents.reason: These are characteristic-class and surgery-theoretic embedding results owned by the later obstruction pages of the DT track, not by the isotopy-extension pair.

contents.name: §2, definition of the modulo 2 Whitney obstruction [Σ(f)] in H_{2n-m}(N;Z_2), its independence of the general-position map, and the nonembeddability criterion
§2, definition of the integral Whitney obstruction for N orientable and m-n odd, in H_{2n-m}(N;Z), with the linking-coefficient description of the signs
§2, definition of the Whitney invariant W(f) in H_{2n-m+1}(N;Z(m-n-1)) and its independence of the general-position homotopy
§2, Theorem 2.8.a: a closed d-connected n-manifold embeds into R^{2n-d-1} if the Whitney obstruction ̄W_{n-d-1} vanishes
contents.reason: The sufficiency direction needs the deleted-product obstruction theory and the disjunction method beyond the design's level; this pair only names the primary obstruction.

contents.name: §2, Theorem 2.8.b: the Whitney invariant is a bijection onto a homology group in the stated range, so the classification of embeddings needs more than the primary class
§2, remark after 2.8.b: because of the existence of knots the analogous classifications below the metastable range are false, and smooth classification is much harder
§3, Example 3.4: the trefoil knot S^{2l-1}→R^{3l} is not smoothly trivial (PL trivial for l≥2)
§3, Examples 3.2–3.3 and 3.5 (Borromean rings, Whitehead link, Haefliger torus)
contents.reason: Higher-dimensional links and knotted tori are the advanced knotting material that the design explicitly leaves to the low-dimensional and knot tracks; DT-27 records the trefoil witness only.

contents.name: §3, Theorems 3.6 and 3.8–3.9 (classification of links of spheres and of knotted tori below the metastable range)
